item.text: {"question_id":"4B.9","answer":"For 2023, Mexico had formal safeguards but materially deficient operational oversight. The Supreme Court upheld a communications-interception framework requiring judicial authorization, specified subjects, places, purposes, duration and offenses, with inventories, judicial verification or revocation, destruction of non-useful information, confidentiality, and certified personnel. It also held general internet monitoring valid only for publicly accessible information and subject to privacy protections. Conversely, the Court invalidated Guardia Nacional undercover and simulated-user powers for lacking defined conditions, a crime catalogue, and prior judicial control. Real-time geolocation remained unresolved because the Court dismissed the challenge for failure to reach the qualified-vote threshold, expressly without deciding constitutionality. Operational evidence was more adverse: investigative and forensic reporting linked Pegasus surveillance of journalists, human-rights defenders, investigators, and officials to military structures; leaked SEDENA materials reportedly showed surveillance of Raymundo Ramos through a secret military-intelligence unit, while the supplied record reports no located judicial-intervention request. Telcel reportedly provided records of more than a dozen officials between 2021 and 2023 in response to Mexico City prosecutor orders without the required judicial authorization, although responsibility was disputed. López Obrador publicly denied or minimized several allegations, and authorities were slow to investigate; INAI’s order to obtain Pegasus contracts was not promptly complied with. These facts support a mixed formal framework alongside serious, ruler-attributable administrative and oversight failures, but they do not prove that López Obrador personally ordered each surveillance operation or establish final accountability outcomes.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0057-E007","BATCH-0057-E005","BATCH-0057-E006","BATCH-0057-E017","BATCH-0014-E006","BATCH-0014-E007","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0030-E002","BATCH-0042-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0057-E008","BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0010-E001","BATCH-0026-E015","BATCH-0055-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The surveillance evidence includes investigative, leaked-document, forensic, and advocacy reporting; some attribution remains reported or inferential rather than finally adjudicated.","The record does not establish López Obrador’s personal authorization of specific operations, complete accountability outcomes, or the final disposition of all investigations.","The Telcel disclosures span 2021–2023, not solely 2023, and the supplied source reports disputed responsibility.","Formal legal safeguards and court rulings establish the framework, not proof that every 2023 operation complied with it."],"corrections_made":["Separated formal statutory safeguards from actual surveillance and enforcement practice.","Recast the Pegasus and Ramos evidence as reported or investigative findings, with attribution limited to military structures and senior-defense-chain awareness where supported.","Added the Telcel disclosures and clarified that the required judicial authorization was reportedly absent, while preserving disputed responsibility.","Added that the Supreme Court’s real-time-geolocation disposition was procedural and did not decide constitutionality.","Clarified that the undercover-operation ruling concerned statutory authority and did not itself prove a specific operation.","Limited attribution of presidential responsibility to López Obrador’s public denials, minimization, and administration-level institutional environment."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A final, independent determination of responsibility and legality for the Pegasus, Ramos, Encinas, and Telcel episodes could materially refine the operational-oversight assessment.","Additional records on compliance with judicial authorizations, INAI enforcement, investigations, sanctions, remedies, and geolocation implementation would reduce uncertainty."]}
